newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - May 22.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - May 22.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
BONN - The German advertising industry should have a new quality-control system in place by October for inspecting billboards, industry watchdog group IVW says. (Reuter)

BONN - German free newspapers posted moderate growth in advertising income for the second year in a row in 1996, an industry association says. With a 3.2 percent climb in ad income to 3.011 billion marks ($1.8 billion), the association of German advertising pages (BVDA) says the relatively slow expansion reflected the weakness of the country's retail market. (Reuter)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

BONN - Media companies and politicians taking part in the cable and digital television summit describe it as a partial success. A spokesman from the Kirch-Gruppe says he is pleased that Deutsche Telekom plans to make public its prices for the distribution of digital programming over its cable network.
(Reuter)

LUDWIGSHAFEN - State media authorities warn that Deutsche Telekom is growing too powerful in the development of digital television. Because of Telekom's control satellite and cable networks, free communication could be endangered. (Reuter)
WALLDORF - Gruner & Jahr sells their women's magazine Prima Carina, effective August 1, 1997, for a seven-figure price to Klambt-Verlag of Speyer. (Kress)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

MUNICH - SKW Trostberg AG, the world's largest construction chemicals firm, says its sales were climbing so far this year but warned a major acquistion in 1996 could hurt net profit. SKW said in a statement that sales climbed 37 percent in the first quarter of 1997 to 1.32 billion marks, but that without the purchase last autumn of Master Builders Technologies turnover would have climbed only four percent. (Reuter)
HAMBURG - A controlling stake in German supermarket chain Spar Handels AG has been bought by a group led by France's Intermarche, sellers' group NHH Norddeutsche Handels Holding GmbH says. (Reuter)
HAMBURG - Specialty chemicals and consumer products group Beiersdorf AG says it increased its turnover by 6.8 percent worldwide in the first four months of 1997. (Reuter)

FLENSBURG - Turnover in shipping trade in the first quarter of 1997 sank 3.8 percent from the previous year, the association of German shipping trade (BVH) says based on a poll it conducted. (Handelsblatt)
BREMEN - Coffee roaster Jacobs will decide in the next feww weeks if its coffee prices will further increase. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:
FRANKFURT - NBC Europe has named Allan Horlick as new president and managing director. Horlick is currently the chief executive of WCR-TV, the Washington NBC affiliate. (Horizont)
